questions.q: we're feeding user-supplied config in — is there anything stopping a deeply nested array from blowing the stack?
questions.why: parser/mod.rs defines `const LIMIT: u32 = 80` and wraps the event receiver in `RecursionGuard::new(&mut receiver, LIMIT)` unless the `unbounded` feature is on; key.rs re-checks the same LIMIT against dotted-key path length and reports 'recursion limit'.

questions.q: when I serialize a Vec of structs, what decides whether I get [[items]] sections or one long inline array?
questions.why: `SerializationStrategy` + the `WalkValue` probe serializer; `ArrayWalkValue::end` returns `ArrayOfTables` when the seq is non-empty and every element walked as a Table, otherwise `Value`.

questions.q: writing an inline table, why doesn't a None field abort the whole thing with 'unsupported None value'?
questions.why: `MapValueSerializer::serialize_none` sets the `is_none` flag before erroring, and `SerializeTable::serialize_value`/`serialize_field` swallow the error only when `e == Error::unsupported_none() && is_none`.

questions.q: the parse errors print a little caret diagram — where's the code that turns a byte offset into that?
questions.why: `translate_position` maps a byte index to (line, column) and the `Display for Error` impl writes the 'TOML parse error at line N, column M' block with the gutter and `^` underline.

questions.q: are table keys stored sorted or in the order they appeared, and can I switch that?
questions.why: `type MapImpl<K, V>` is a `BTreeMap` by default and an `IndexMap` under `preserve_order`; `fast_hash` swaps the hasher to foldhash. `remove`/`remove_entry` also switch to `shift_remove` in that mode.

questions.q: I want to report every syntax problem in a file, not just bail on the first one — is that possible?
questions.why: `DeTable::parse_recoverable` returns `(Spanned<Self>, Vec<Error>)` using `TomlSink::<Vec<_>>`; error.rs has the two `ErrorSink` impls, one that keeps only the first error and one that pushes all of them.

questions.q: which code rejects `a.b.c = 1` when `[a.b]` was already written earlier in the file?
questions.why: `descend_path` reports 'duplicate key' when `dotted && !sweet_child_of_mine.is_implicit()`, and `capture_key_value` / `start_table` do the matching implicit-vs-explicit table checks.

questions.q: what happens if a TOML integer doesn't fit in i64 — hard error or does it try wider types?
questions.why: `ValueDeserializer::deserialize_any` tries to_i64, then to_u64, then to_i128, then to_u128 before 'integer number overflowed'; devalue.rs holds those `from_str_radix` helpers on `DeInteger`.

questions.q: if the source said 0xdeadbeef, can I still tell it was hex after parsing?
questions.why: `DeInteger` keeps `inner: Cow<str>` plus a `radix: u32`, exposed via `as_str()`/`radix()`, and its Display re-prefixes 0b/0o/0x based on the radix.

questions.q: my config type is a HashMap<u32, T> — how does the string key become a number?
questions.why: `KeyDeserializer` implements deserialize_u8..u128/i8..i128/bool/char by `self.key.parse()` and forwarding to the parsed value's own deserializer.

questions.q: we get `nan` and never `-nan` in output — is that deliberate?
questions.why: both `ValueSerializer::serialize_f32`/`serialize_f64` in ser/value/mod.rs and `value::ValueSerializer::serialize_f64` call `value.copysign(1.0)` when `is_nan()`, with a comment explaining the sign is discarded.

questions.q: where does the one-element-per-line array formatting actually get switched on and applied?
questions.why: `Serializer::pretty` sets `style.multiline_array = true`; `SerializeValueArray::multiline_array()` gates on that plus `2 <= len`, and emits newline + 4 spaces per element with a trailing comma.

questions.q: why does a struct whose fields are all sub-structs not get its own [header] line in the output?
questions.why: `required_table()` keeps a keyed table only if `table.array || !table.body.is_empty() || !table.has_children`; `child_table` sets `has_children` on the parent.

questions.q: what does a Vec<u8> turn into — a string, or something else?
questions.why: `value::ValueSerializer::serialize_bytes` maps each byte to `Value::Integer` producing an array; ser/value/mod.rs's `serialize_bytes` just re-serializes the slice, which lands in the array writer.

questions.q: internally, how does a parsed array remember it came from [[headers]] rather than being a literal `[...]`?
questions.why: `DeArray` carries a private `array_of_tables: bool` with `is_array_of_tables()`/`set_array_of_tables()`; document.rs's `finish_table` sets it when creating the entry and refuses to push into an array where it is false.

questions.q: I'm getting 'map key was not a string' on serialize — where is that raised?
questions.why: table.rs's `SerializeMap::serialize_key` returns `Error::key_not_string()` for any non-`Value::String` key; ser/value/key.rs's `KeySerializer` returns the same for floats, bytes, seqs, maps, None, units etc.

questions.q: is there a way to write a literal TOML table in Rust source without parsing a string at runtime?
questions.why: the exported `toml!` macro plus the `toml_internal!` tt-muncher, backed by `insert_toml`, `push_toml` and `traverse` helpers at the bottom of the file.

questions.q: for a tuple enum variant, can the data come from a table instead of an array, and what are the key rules?
questions.why: `TableEnumDeserializer::tuple_variant` accepts a table only if key N parses as usize and equals its positional index, erroring with 'expected table key `{index}`, but was `{key}`'.

questions.q: does `{a = 1, a = 2}` get caught, and where?
questions.why: `State::finish_value` matches on `table.entry(key)` and reports 'duplicate key' with both spans on `Entry::Occupied`; its `descend_path` handles the dotted-key-inside-inline-table cases.

questions.q: where in the parse path does a datetime-looking scalar get turned into a Datetime value?
questions.why: `on_scalar` matches `ScalarKind::DateTime` and does `decoded.parse::<toml_datetime::Datetime>()`, reporting a ParseError and substituting an all-None Datetime on failure.
